question: Should OpenClaw accept this external PR's `acpx@0.12.0` dependency graph change after direct ACPX proof, or require exact-head OpenClaw Gateway proof and maintainer-owned dependency approval first?
rationale: The branch changes package manifests and lockfiles for code that launches external ACP agent processes and handles provider credentials, and direct ACPX proof does not by itself settle the OpenClaw Gateway integration or security approval boundary.

options.title: Approve After OpenClaw Proof
options.body: Require redacted `/acp spawn grok-build` or `sessions_spawn` proof on this head, then let admin/security approve the exact dependency-change SHA if the package delta is acceptable.

options.title: Regenerate Internally
options.body: Have maintainers recreate the `acpx@0.12.0` package and lockfile update from a trusted branch while preserving the contributor's docs and routing fixes as reference.

options.title: Accept Direct ACPX Proof
options.body: A maintainer may explicitly waive Gateway proof and accept the direct WSL `acpx@0.12.0 grok-build` smoke plus dependency review as enough for this release.

recommendation.title: Approve After OpenClaw Proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted `/acp spawn grok-build` or `sessions_spawn` proof on this head, then let admin/security approve the exact dependency-change SHA if the package delta is acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: This account landed the upstream ACPX Grok Build release consumed here and has recent history on the matching OpenClaw docs/package surfaces.
